business_model.claim: Kodiak Sciences is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company with no products approved for commercial sale and no revenue since commencing operations in June 2009.
quotes: We commenced operations in June 2009, have no products approved for commercial sale and have not generated any revenue.

business_model.claim: Because it generates no product revenue, Kodiak has historically funded its operations primarily through issuing common stock and selling future royalties.
quotes: We have funded our operations primarily through the issuance of common stock and the sale of future royalties.

business_model.claim: Instead of selling approved products today, Kodiak is developing three late-stage clinical programs and has retained all global rights to make, use, and sell its product candidates.
quotes: We are developing a portfolio of three late-stage clinical programs, two of which are derived from our ABC platform and one which is platform-independent.
To date, we have retained all global rights to make, use and sell our product candidates, which we believe preserves future value and allows for agile decision-making.

business_model.claim: Kodiak's late-stage investigational medicines target patients with retinal diseases: Zenkuda in wet AMD, diabetic retinopathy, and retinal vein occlusion; tabirafusp-ted (KSI-501) in wet AMD and diabetic macular edema; and KSI-101 in macular edema secondary to inflammation.
quotes: Zenkuda (tarcocimab tedromer) has a BLA-ready profile in wet AMD, diabetic retinopathy, and retinal vein occlusion.
KSI-501 is being evaluated in wet AMD and diabetic macular edema.
We are developing KSI-101 for patients with macular edema (retinal fluid) secondary to inflammation (“MESI”).

business_model.claim: Beyond its late-stage candidates, Kodiak is advancing earlier-stage ABCD platform therapies for glaucoma and geographic atrophy, developing an AI-enabled wearable headset called VETi, and operating its URSUS commercial-scale manufacturing facility.
quotes: Our ABCD platform is advancing a next set of investigational therapies for high prevalence retinal diseases, including our novel “duet” technology for glaucoma and geographic atrophy (“GA”).
VETi is our AI- and machine-learning-enabled wearable headset with applications in retina care alongside broader opportunities in identity security and cognitive sciences.

URSUS is a custom-designed premium commercial manufacturing facility dedicated to the large scale manufacture of Kodiak’s ABC medicines, built in collaboration with Lonza, a leading drug contract manufacturing firm.

business_model.claim: Future product revenue depends on clinical trial success, regulatory approval, and commercialization, with Zenkuda and KSI-501 targeting the $15 billion anti-VEGF market and KSI-101 targeting a separate MESI market segment.
quotes: The Company’s ability to achieve and sustain profitability will depend on the successful development, approval and commercialization of its product candidates and on the achievement of sufficient revenue to support its cost structure and, unless and until it does, the Company will need to raise additional capital to maintain current operations and to continue research and development activities.
Zenkuda and KSI-501 target the $15 billion anti-VEGF market across retinal vascular diseases.
MESI represents a new macular edema market segment separate from the established anti-VEGF market.

business_model.claim: Currently, Kodiak earns interest income on its cash and cash equivalents, which moves with the balance of cash available to earn interest and rates of return.
quotes: Interest income consists primarily of interest income earned on our cash and cash equivalents.

Interest income decreased $6.6 million during the year ended December 31, 2025 as compared to 2024, which was attributable to the overall decrease in cash available to earn interest during 2025 combined with lower rates of return.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the third-quarter 2026 10-Q MD&A and third-quarter 2026 8-K earnings release.
competitive_position.claim: Zenkuda and KSI-501 target the $15 billion anti-VEGF market across retinal vascular diseases, with Zenkuda exhibiting a mean ocular half-life in humans of 20 days.
quotes: Zenkuda and KSI-501 target the $15 billion anti-VEGF market across retinal vascular diseases.

Zenkuda has a mean ocular half-life in humans of 20 days, approximately three times longer than approved anti-VEGF therapies and is designed to maintain potent and effective drug levels in ocular tissues for longer.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the September 28, 2026 8-K, third-quarter 2026 10-Q MD&A, and third-quarter 2026 earnings release.
competitive_position.claim: In the pivotal DAYBREAK wet AMD trial, Zenkuda met the non-inferiority primary endpoint (p-value of 0.0007) with 54% of patients on 6-month dosing, a 0% intraocular inflammation rate, and a 0.5% cataract adverse event rate versus 0.9% for aflibercept.
quotes: Zenkuda (tarcocimab tedromer) met the primary endpoint (p-value of 0.0007) demonstrating meaningful vision gains as well as rapid and sustained retinal drying with the majority of patients (54%) on 6-month dosing, establishing a first-line benchmark in wet age-related macular degeneration (wAMD)
Zenkuda demonstrated favorable safety and was well tolerated in the study with a 0% intraocular inflammation rate and a 0.5% cataract adverse event rate (vs 0.9% with aflibercept comparator).

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the third-quarter 2026 10-Q MD&A and third-quarter 2026 earnings release.
competitive_position.claim: Zenkuda successfully treated diabetic retinopathy in the GLOW1 and GLOW2 trials with 100% of patients on extended 6-month dosing at Year 1 and completed pivotal RVO (BEACON) and wet AMD (DAYLIGHT) studies ahead of a planned multi-indication BLA submission in the fourth quarter of 2026.
quotes: In the GLOW1 and GLOW2 studies, Zenkuda successfully treated DR patients and prevented disease progression with 100% of patients on extended 6-month dosing at Year 1.
We are planning to submit a three-indication (wet AMD, DR, and RVO) biologics license application (“BLA”) for Zenkuda in the fourth quarter of 2026.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 10-K and third-quarter 2026 10-Q Risk Factors.
competitive_position.claim: Previously, tarcocimab failed to meet primary non-inferiority visual acuity endpoints in the DAZZLE wet AMD trial and the GLEAM and GLIMMER DME trials, where an unexpected increase in cataracts was observed and led to a temporary development pause in 2023.
quotes: For example, in our Phase 2b/3 DAZZLE clinical trial evaluating the efficacy, durability and safety of tarcocimab in treatment-naïve subjects with neovascular wet AMD and in our Phase 3 GLEAM and GLIMMER studies, tarcocimab did not meet the primary efficacy endpoint of showing non-inferior visual acuity gains.

For example, in the tarcocimab arms of our completed GLEAM and GLIMMER clinical trials, we observed an unexpected increase in cataracts, which we believe may have contributed meaningfully to the failure of each study to meet its primary efficacy endpoint.

In July 2023, we announced that the Phase 3 GLEAM and GLIMMER clinical trials of tarcocimab did not meet their primary efficacy endpoints and, as a result, we paused further development of tarcocimab pending review of Year 1 data from the Phase 3 BEACON study in patients with RVO and the Phase 3 GLOW1 study of patients with DR.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the third-quarter 2026 10-Q MD&A, third-quarter 2026 earnings release, and September 28, 2026 8-K.
competitive_position.claim: Kodiak's second late-stage candidate, tabirafusp-ted (KSI-501), is a bispecific anti-IL-6 and VEGF-trap therapy that met both its vision primary endpoint (p-value of 0.0036) and anatomical key secondary endpoint (p-value of <0.0001) in DAYBREAK and is enrolling in the ALTO DME superiority trial against aflibercept.
quotes: In the DAYBREAK study, tabirafusp-ted met the vision primary endpoint (p-value of 0.0036) and anatomical key secondary endpoint (p-value of <0.0001).

Kodiak has also advanced tabirafusp-ted into the registrational Phase 3 ALTO study designed to explore the superiority of bispecific tabirafusp-ted (anti-VEGF, anti-IL-6) versus monospecific aflibercept (anti-VEGF) in patients with diabetic macular edema (“DME”).

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the third-quarter 2026 10-Q MD&A and third-quarter 2026 earnings release.
competitive_position.claim: KSI-101 targets macular edema secondary to inflammation (MESI), a market segment separate from anti-VEGF with no currently available intravitreal biologic therapies, after ≥90% of top-dose patients in the APEX study achieved complete absence of intraretinal and subretinal fluid.
quotes: Currently there are no available intravitreal biologic therapies addressing the spectrum of MESI diseases.
MESI represents a new macular edema market segment separate from the established anti-VEGF market.
In top dose groups, ≥90% achieved complete absence of IRF and SRF, indicating retinal dryness and normalization of retinal architecture.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 10-K MD&A and third-quarter 2026 10-Q MD&A.
competitive_position.claim: Beyond its late-stage candidates, Kodiak is developing the ABCD small-molecule conjugation platform—including glaucoma and geographic atrophy duet programs aiming for quarterly dosing versus monthly or every-other-month approved GA therapies—alongside pre-IND bispecifics and the VETi AI headset.
quotes: The objective of this duet program is to create an intravitreally injected ABCD platform-enabled therapy with a dual mechanism of action to achieve better efficacy and extended durability, for quarterly dosing, as compared to currently approved therapies for GA, which are based on a single mechanism of action and are dosed monthly or every other month.
VETi is our AI- and machine-learning-enabled wearable headset with applications in retina care alongside broader opportunities in identity security and cognitive sciences.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 10-K and third-quarter 2026 10-Q Risk Factors.
competitive_position.claim: Kodiak has never submitted a BLA, creating risk that the FDA or foreign regulators delay, reject, or narrow labeling and dosing claims—including requiring separate review of DAYBREAK's AI-based dosing tool or questioning formulation bridging.
quotes: We have never submitted a BLA, and even if GLOW1, GLOW2, BEACON, DAYLIGHT or DAYBREAK clinical data support submission of a tarcocimab BLA to the FDA in 2026, we may need to delay submission which would delay review and potential approval.

For example, our DAYBREAK trial uses an AI-based tool to measure retinal fluid and individualize dosing, and this dosing may not be incorporated into labeling or may require separate FDA review of the AI-based tool.

While the FDA has advised that the additional clinical studies to be conducted with the revised formulation should be sufficient to bridge the former material to the go-to-market material, we cannot be sure that the FDA, EMA or comparable foreign regulatory authorities would agree or accept our planned BLA even if our planned additional trials are successful and, as a result, further development of tarcocimab and KSI-501 may ultimately not be successful.

our competitors may develop platform technologies that render our ABC Platform obsolete or less attractive;

any product candidates and the ABC Platform that we develop may not be sufficiently covered by intellectual property for which we hold exclusive rights or may be covered by third party patents or other intellectual property or exclusive rights;

if a product candidate obtains regulatory approval, we may be unable to establish sales and marketing capabilities, or successfully market such approved product candidate, to gain market acceptance; and

Clinical trial delays could also shorten any periods during which our products have patent protection and may allow our competitors to bring products to market before we do, which could impair our ability to successfully commercialize our product candidates and may harm our business and results of operations.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 10-K and third-quarter 2026 10-Q Risk Factors.

Our previous clinical trial results are not necessarily predictive of the results of our on-going or future discovery programs or any future preclinical or clinical studies.

growth_thesis.claim: Zenkuda targets the $15 billion anti-VEGF market across wet AMD, diabetic retinopathy, and retinal vein occlusion, with 54% of DAYBREAK patients on 6-month dosing and a multi-indication BLA planned for 4Q2026.
quotes: Zenkuda and KSI-501 target the $15 billion anti-VEGF market across retinal vascular diseases.

Zenkuda met the primary endpoint (p-value of 0.0007) demonstrating meaningful vision gains as well as rapid and sustained retinal drying with the majority of patients (54%) on 6-month dosing, establishing a first-line benchmark in wet age-related macular degeneration (wet AMD).

Kodiak plans to submit Zenkuda data to regulatory authorities in 4Q2026 from five positive Phase 3 studies, DAYBREAK and DAYLIGHT in wAMD, GLOW and GLOW2 in diabetic retinopathy (DR) and BEACON in macular edema following retinal vein occlusion (RVO).

growth_thesis.claim: For Zenkuda to generate commercial growth, Kodiak must submit its initial BLA in 2026 and obtain FDA acceptance and approval across the target indications and extended dosing label.
quotes: We have never submitted a BLA, and even if GLOW1, GLOW2, BEACON, DAYLIGHT or DAYBREAK clinical data support submission of a tarcocimab BLA to the FDA in 2026, we may need to delay submission which would delay review and potential approval.
FDA may not approve a label for a particular dosing frequency, even if we believe the data demonstrate support for that dosing.

For example, our DAYBREAK trial uses an AI-based tool to measure retinal fluid and individualize dosing, and this dosing may not be incorporated into labeling or may require separate FDA review of the AI-based tool.

While the FDA has advised that the additional clinical studies to be conducted with the revised formulation should be sufficient to bridge the former material to the go-to-market material, we cannot be sure that the FDA, EMA or comparable foreign regulatory authorities would agree or accept our planned BLA even if our planned additional trials are successful and, as a result, further development of tarcocimab and KSI-501 may ultimately not be successful.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in 10-Q MD&A [P5] and 8-K earnings release [P8].
growth_thesis.claim: Tabirafusp-ted targets the $15 billion anti-VEGF market with dual IL-6 and VEGF inhibition, having met its vision and anatomical endpoints in DAYBREAK for wet AMD while enrolling the ALTO trial in diabetic macular edema.
quotes: Tabirafusp alfa tedromer ("tabirafusp-ted" or “KSI-501”), our second investigational medicine, is an anti-IL-6, VEGF-trap bispecific therapy built on the ABC platform and is being developed for high prevalence retinal vascular diseases to address the leading unmet needs of extended durability and targeting disease biology beyond VEGF for differentiated efficacy.
In the DAYBREAK study, tabirafusp-ted met the vision primary endpoint (p-value of 0.0036) and anatomical key secondary endpoint (p-value of <0.0001).

Kodiak has also advanced tabirafusp-ted into the registrational Phase 3 ALTO study designed to explore the superiority of bispecific tabirafusp-ted (anti-VEGF, anti-IL-6) versus monospecific aflibercept (anti-VEGF) in patients with diabetic macular edema (“DME”).
Zenkuda and KSI-501 target the $15 billion anti-VEGF market across retinal vascular diseases.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in 10-Q Risk Factors [P6] and 8-K earnings release [P8].
growth_thesis.claim: For tabirafusp-ted to expand Kodiak's growth beyond anti-VEGF monotherapy, ongoing DAYBREAK follow-up, subgroup analyses, and the ALTO DME trial must confirm differentiated IL-6 plus VEGF efficacy and earn regulatory approval.
quotes: Post-hoc analyses to identify which treatment naïve wet AMD patient sub-groups can benefit from IL-6 inhibition are planned.

The ongoing second year of the DAYBREAK study will further assess the long-term efficacy profile of tabirafusp-ted and explore whether dual inhibition of IL-6 and VEGF can deliver additional benefits for specific patient groups within the study’s broad treatment-naïve wet AMD population.
We cannot be certain that our product candidates will be successful in any of the planned or pending clinical trials.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in 10-Q MD&A [P5] and 8-K earnings release [P8].
growth_thesis.claim: KSI-101 targets MESI as a separate market segment with no available intravitreal biologic therapies, with initial PEAK topline results expected in December 2026 and a planned BLA submission in 2027.
quotes: Currently there are no available intravitreal biologic therapies addressing the spectrum of MESI diseases.
MESI represents a new macular edema market segment separate from the established anti-VEGF market.
Enrollment of the first 300-patient cohort in the PEAK trial supporting Pivotal Analysis 1 has completed and topline results remain on track for a December 2026 release.
Topline data for Pivotal Analysis 1 (PEAK) are expected in December 2026 and Pivotal Analysis 2 (PEAK+PINNACLE) in 2Q 2027.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in 10-K Risk Factors [P2], 10-Q MD&A [P5], and 10-Q Risk Factors [P6].
growth_thesis.claim: For KSI-101 to become a growth driver, PEAK and PINNACLE must complete enrollment and demonstrate superiority over sham treatment in efficacy and safety to support BLA approval.
quotes: The PEAK and PINNACLE studies are superiority studies evaluating two dose levels of KSI-101 (5 mg and 10 mg) compared to sham treatment in patients with MESI.
We cannot guarantee that any clinical trials will be conducted as planned or completed on schedule, if at all.
Any clinical studies that we may conduct may not demonstrate the efficacy and safety necessary to obtain regulatory approval to market our product candidates.

growth_thesis.claim: Beyond its late-stage trials, Kodiak is developing pre-IND bispecific antibodies (KSI-102 and KSI-103), small-molecule ABCD duet programs for glaucoma and geographic atrophy, and the VETi AI-enabled wearable headset.
quotes: With regards to our pipeline programs, dual cytokine-targeting bispecific antibody programs KSI-102 (anti-TNFa/IL-6) and KSI-103 (anti-IL-1/IL-6) continue to progress through pre-IND activities, targeting diseases of ocular inflammation.
Our ABCD platform is advancing a next set of investigational therapies for high prevalence retinal diseases, including our novel “duet” technology for glaucoma and geographic atrophy (“GA”).
VETi is our AI- and machine-learning-enabled wearable headset with applications in retina care alongside broader opportunities in identity security and cognitive sciences.

growth_thesis.claim: For Kodiak's earlier-stage pipeline and ABC/ABCD platform extensions to contribute to growth, they require substantial additional time and investment to advance through preclinical and clinical testing without failing or being outcompeted.
quotes: It will take additional investment and time for such programs to reach the same stage of development as tarcocimab, KSI-501 and KSI-101.

Failure of a product candidate may occur at any stage of preclinical or clinical development, and, because our product candidates and our ABC Platform are in development, there is a relatively higher risk of failure and we may never succeed in developing marketable products or generating product revenue.

quotes: URSUS is a custom-designed premium commercial manufacturing facility dedicated to the large scale manufacture of Kodiak’s ABC medicines, built in collaboration with Lonza, a leading drug contract manufacturing firm.
To date, we have retained all global rights to make, use and sell our product candidates, which we believe preserves future value and allows for agile decision-making.

growth_thesis.claim: To convert approved candidates and URSUS capacity into revenue growth, Kodiak must validate commercial manufacturing at acceptable cost, reach CMC agreement with regulators, and build commercial sales and marketing capabilities.
quotes: To date, we have not obtained marketing approval for any of our product candidates or conducted sales and marketing activities necessary for successful product commercialization.

We may also face delays if we are unable to reach agreement with the FDA, EMA or other regulatory authorities regarding CMC matters, including methodologies for, and assessment of, comparability of manufacturing procedures and lots.

Even if we receive regulatory approval to market any of our product candidates, we cannot assure you that any such product candidate will be successfully commercialized, widely accepted in the marketplace or more effective than other commercially available alternatives.

growth_thesis.claim: To avoid pausing or scaling back development programs, Kodiak must raise additional capital, as management disclosed substantial doubt about continuing as a going concern with $88.7 million in cash and cash equivalents at the end of the third quarter of 2026, prior to $69 million in subsequent ATM proceeds.
quotes: Kodiak ended the third quarter of 2026 with $88.7 million of cash and cash equivalents.
Subsequent to September 30, 2026, Kodiak raised aggregate net proceeds of $69 million through sales of common stock under its ATM equity offering facility.

The Company believes that the existing cash and cash equivalents may not be sufficient to meet the anticipated operating and capital expenditure requirements for the 12 months following the date of this Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q.
As a result, there is substantial doubt regarding the Company's ability to continue as a going concern.
If we are unable to raise additional funds when needed, we may be required to pause, scale back or discontinue one or more of our development programs.

material_events.claim: Kodiak announced that Zenkuda and tabirafusp-ted met their primary endpoints in the DAYBREAK wet age-related macular degeneration study, with p-values of 0.0007 and 0.0036, respectively.
quotes: On September 28, 2026, Kodiak Sciences Inc. (the “Company”) issued a press release announcing that the primary endpoints were met for both Zenkuda (tarcocimab tedromer) and tabirafusp-ted (KSI-501) in the Company’s Phase 3 DAYBREAK study in patients with wet age-related macular degeneration.

Zenkuda met the primary endpoint (p-value of 0.0007) demonstrating meaningful vision gains as well as rapid and sustained retinal drying with the majority of patients (54%) on 6-month dosing, establishing a first-line benchmark in wet age-related macular degeneration (wet AMD).
Tabirafusp-ted met the vision primary endpoint (p-value of 0.0036) and anatomical key secondary endpoint (p-value of <0.0001).

In GLOW2, Zenkuda met its primary endpoint of the proportion of patients with at least a 2-step improvement on the DRSS, with 62.5% of Zenkuda-treated patients demonstrating at least a 2-step improvement versus 3.3% of patients in the sham group, a 19-fold increased response rate ratio (p-value < 0.0001).

material_events.claim: Kodiak announced that the GLEAM and GLIMMER studies of tarcocimab in diabetic macular edema did not meet their primary efficacy endpoints and paused further development of tarcocimab.
quotes: On July 24, 2023, Kodiak announced that although high proportions of patients on meaningfully longer treatment intervals were observed with tarcocimab, with half of patients on every 24-week dosing at the primary endpoint, the GLEAM and GLIMMER studies did not meet their primary efficacy endpoints of showing non-inferior visual acuity gains for tarcocimab dosed every 8 to 24 weeks after 3 monthly loading doses compared to aflibercept given every 8 weeks after 5 monthly loading doses.

In July 2023, we announced that the Phase 3 GLEAM and GLIMMER clinical trials of tarcocimab did not meet their primary efficacy endpoints and, as a result, we paused further development of tarcocimab pending review of Year 1 data from the Phase 3 BEACON study in patients with RVO and the Phase 3 GLOW1 study of patients with DR.

risks.claim: Ongoing or future clinical trials of Zenkuda, tabirafusp-ted, and KSI-101 could fail to meet efficacy endpoints or exhibit adverse events, echoing earlier trial failures in DAZZLE, GLEAM, and GLIMMER.
quotes: For example, in our Phase 2b/3 DAZZLE clinical trial evaluating the efficacy, durability and safety of tarcocimab in treatment-naïve subjects with neovascular wet AMD and in our Phase 3 GLEAM and GLIMMER studies, tarcocimab did not meet the primary efficacy endpoint of showing non-inferior visual acuity gains.

For example, in the tarcocimab arms of our completed GLEAM and GLIMMER clinical trials, we observed an unexpected increase in cataracts, which we believe may have contributed meaningfully to the failure of each study to meet its primary efficacy endpoint.
The DAYBREAK study in wAMD demonstrated that both Zenkuda and tabirafusp-ted achieved non-inferiority in vision gains compared to aflibercept at year one.
